title: A Machine for the Protocol
premise: When Oscar Underhill answers a distress beacon broadcast in dead High Meridian, he finds the derelict station Vespergate and a survivor, Ilse Vann, who claims the station's crew was massacred by the Charter Fleet — a crime erased from every ledger, including the insurance records Oscar himself once certified. To prove the massacre happened, Oscar and Ilse must recover the station's black box from the Fleet's evidence vaults before Earth's final transmission loop, the Protocol, expires and seals all contested-orbit claims forever. Along the way Oscar discovers his own late father helped write the erasure, trading justice for the family's shipping license. In the end Oscar broadcasts the raw black box through the Protocol's own authentication channel — an act of piracy that costs him his license and nearly his life, but forces the Fleet to acknowledge Vespergate, and leaves Ilse, not the courts, holding the truth as inheritance.
about_author: Theo Zhou is a former maritime claims adjuster who spent six years aboard research vessels in the South China Sea before turning to fiction. He writes about paperwork, grief, and the machinery that decides whose losses count.

chapters.title: Dead Language, Live Signal
chapters.summary: Oscar Underhill, hauling insurance cargo through contested orbits, intercepts a distress ping in High Meridian, a language extinct two centuries. His ship's protocol flags it as impossible. POV Oscar. Beat: restless competence cracked open by wonder — the first anomaly in twelve years of routine.

chapters.title: The Underhill Clause
chapters.summary: Oscar's employer, Corvane Mutual, orders him to log the signal as sensor ghost and move on; his contract's fine print gives them ownership of anything he finds. He logs it — and secretly copies the coordinates. POV Oscar. Beat: quiet rebellion born of a man tired of certifying other people's losses.

chapters.title: Vespergate
chapters.summary: Oscar docks at the derelict station Vespergate, finding corridors scorched in patterns no accident produces and a med-bay sealed from the inside. He knows impossible accidents for a living; this is one. POV Oscar. Beat: dread mounting as expertise confirms what hope denies.

chapters.title: Ilse Vann, Sole Survivor
chapters.summary: Oscar finds Ilse Vann hiding in the hydroponics ring, half-starved, speaking accented High Meridian. She says the Charter Fleet fired on the station and then rewrote the record. POV Ilse. Beat: feral distrust slowly yielding to desperate necessity.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Ilse shows Oscar the station's public record: Vespergate's crew died in a 'cascade decompression,' signed off by an adjuster — Oscar's own certification seal, from a report he never filed. POV Ilse. Beat: betrayal; the machinery of his honest life revealed as complicit.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: Oscar recalls his father Aldous, a Corvane founder, and the license that built their name. He begins pulling the threads of his own signed past. POV Oscar. Beat: grief curdling into suspicion about inheritance — what exactly did his father leave him?

chapters.title: The Protocol
chapters.summary: Ilse explains the stakes: Earth's last transmission loop, the Protocol, expires in forty days, after which all contested-orbit claims are permanently closed. Prove the massacre before then, or it never legally happened. POV Ilse. Beat: the clock starts; despair converted into direction.

chapters.title: Charter Patrol at Kessel Drift
chapters.summary: A Fleet patrol vessel hails Oscar's freighter for inspection. He bluffs his way through with genuine Corvane paperwork, hiding Ilse in a coolant tank. POV Oscar. Beat: white-knuckle tension; first direct contact with the power that erased Vespergate.

chapters.title: The Evidence Vault at Meridian Deep
chapters.summary: Ilse reveals the station's black box was seized as 'Fleet evidence' and stored in the vault at Meridian Deep, a fortress station run by Fleet Auditor General Sarn Hale. Getting it out is impossible. POV Ilse. Beat: the plan takes shape against all odds.

chapters.title: An Adjuster's Education
chapters.summary: Oscar teaches Ilse how insurance logic works — how erasures are structured, where seams show. She teaches him Meridian mourning rites for the dead crew. POV alternating. Beat: partnership forming; grief given ritual and shape.

chapters.title: The Broker of Small Crimes
chapters.summary: They hire Dree Okafor, a smuggler with vault-access codes and no loyalties, at the freeport of Ceres Reach. Dree names an obscene price: the coordinates of a Corvane dead-drop Oscar's father used. POV Dree. Beat: uneasy alliance; everyone is selling something.

chapters.title: Aldous Underhill's Dead-Drop
chapters.summary: The dead-drop yields Aldous's private correspondence: he co-authored the Vespergate erasure, trading truth for the family charter. Oscar reads his father's handwriting justifying it as 'market stability.' POV Oscar. Beat: the theme of inheritance lands — the father's legacy is a lie Oscar must spend.

chapters.title: Forty Days, Thirty-Seven Left
chapters.summary: En route to Meridian Deep, the Fleet boards Dree's tug on a pretext. Ilse is nearly identified; Oscar burns a favor from an old claims contact to buy them out. POV Ilse. Beat: the noose tightening; the cost of the mission becomes personal.

chapters.title: Sarn Hale, Keeper of Records
chapters.summary: Inside Meridian Deep under cargo cover, Oscar glimpses Auditor General Hale — a meticulous, courteous man who personally certifies every erasure and sleeps soundly. POV Oscar. Beat: the antagonist introduced as order itself, not cruelty; power that believes it is justice.

chapters.title: The Vault's Architecture
chapters.summary: Dree maps the vault: three authentication layers, the last keyed to the Protocol's master loop — meaning the black box can only be released or destroyed when the Protocol expires. There is a window, and it is closing. POV Dree. Beat: the plan's shape and its terrifying deadline.

chapters.title: A Certified Accident
chapters.summary: Oscar, posing as a Corvane auditor, inspects a Fleet 'accident' aboard Meridian Deep — and recognizes the same forged signature pattern used on Vespergate. The erasure is a template, used dozens of times. POV Oscar. Beat: horror scaling up; one massacre is a policy, not an event.

chapters.title: The Widow in Bay Nine
chapters.summary: A dockworker, Maren, recognizes Ilse's surname — her sister crewed Vespergate. Maren joins them, bringing the dockworkers' silent network as cover. POV Maren. Beat: solidarity from below; the erased dead still have kin.

chapters.title: Hale Takes Notice
chapters.summary: Hale flags Oscar's inspection credentials as a day too fresh. He invites Oscar to dinner — courteous, probing, offering him a partnership in 'managing difficult truths.' POV Hale. Beat: temptation and menace in the same voice; Oscar sees his possible future.

chapters.title: Refusal at Dinner
chapters.summary: Oscar declines Hale's offer, carefully, claiming loyalty to Corvane. Hale lets him leave — and quietly revokes his certification seal. Oscar is now professionally nobody. POV Oscar. Beat: the point of no return; the old life amputated.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Days
chapters.summary: Stripped of credentials, Oscar can no longer bluff. Ilse proposes the heresy: don't steal the black box — authenticate to it, using Aldous's co-author signature on the erasure order itself. The father's crime becomes the key. POV Ilse. Beat: dark ingenuity; inheritance weaponized.

chapters.title: Forging a Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Oscar practices his father's authentication cadence from the correspondence samples — biometric-adjacent, ritual, humiliating. Dree drills them on the vault's timing. POV Oscar. Beat: intimate struggle; literally performing the father he resents.

chapters.title: The Dockworkers' Strike
chapters.summary: Maren's network slows Meridian Deep's cargo flow to cover their insertion window — a labor action the Fleet reads as routine. POV Maren. Beat: collective courage; ordinary people bending the machine.

chapters.title: Insertion
chapters.summary: Oscar and Dree enter the vault's maintenance spine during a pressure-cycle. Ilse runs comms from the tug. Everything holds — until a sensor ghost, the same one Corvane logged, flickers on the vault board. POV Oscar. Beat: breathless procedural tension.

chapters.title: The Black Box Speaks
chapters.summary: Using Aldous's signature, Oscar reaches the box. It plays: Fleet guns, forty-one crew, a captain's last words in High Meridian. Ilse hears her brother's voice. POV Ilse. Beat: the massacre becomes undeniable; grief and vindication in one breath.

chapters.title: Hale Springs the Trap
chapters.summary: The vault seals. Hale, on the intercom, reveals he let them in — to catch them in the act and destroy the box 'legally,' with witnesses. POV Hale. Beat: the antagonist's triumph; order about to consume truth.

chapters.title: Dree's Price
chapters.summary: Dree sacrifices her escape route to blow the maintenance spine open, buying Oscar and the copied box a way out — and staying behind, arrested. Her fee was never the coordinates; it was making the Fleet bleed for once. POV Dree. Beat: costly loyalty; the plan survives at human price.

chapters.title: Fifteen Days, Running
chapters.summary: Fugitives now, they run for a transmission point strong enough to carry the black box through the Protocol's authentication channel — a Fleet-controlled relay at Thessaly Gate. POV Ilse. Beat: exhausted momentum; the endgame in sight.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvane finds Oscar, offering to restore everything — license, name, his father's honor — if he surrenders the box. They invoke his inheritance directly. POV Oscar. Beat: the final temptation; the whole book's question made explicit.

chapters.title: What Inheritance Means
chapters.summary: Oscar refuses, telling the Corvane envoy his father left him a debt, not an estate — and debts get paid. Ilse, listening, finally trusts him completely. POV Ilse. Beat: character resolved; love and conviction aligned.

chapters.title: Maren's Network Rises
chapters.summary: News of Dree's arrest spreads through the docks. Maren's people coordinate a system-wide slow-down to cover the Thessaly run. POV Maren. Beat: the theme of justice outside the law made flesh — the erased organize.

chapters.title: Hale's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Hale faces his own ledger: destroying the box openly would require admitting it exists. His perfect order demands a crime to stay perfect. POV Hale. Beat: antagonist complexity; the corruption of power shown from inside.

chapters.title: The Thessaly Gauntlet
chapters.summary: The run to Thessaly Gate under Fleet interdiction. Dree's tug, Maren's decoys, and Oscar's knowledge of insurance routing lanes thread them through. POV Oscar. Beat: full-velocity action; every ally's contribution paying off.

chapters.title: The Relay
chapters.summary: They seize the relay control room. The Protocol loop has six days left. Uploading requires authentication — and the channel will accept either Aldous's signature or Hale's master key, not both. POV Ilse. Beat: the final mechanism revealed; one move left.

chapters.title: Hale Arrives
chapters.summary: Hale comes personally, offering Oscar the master key in exchange for co-authorship: broadcast the massacre, but framed as a rogue commander's act, leaving the system intact. Justice, laundered. POV Hale. Beat: the climax of ideas — partial justice offered as mercy.

chapters.title: The Raw Broadcast
chapters.summary: Oscar and Ilse choose the whole truth: they broadcast the black box unedited, unframed, in High Meridian and trade-tongue both, through Aldous's signature. The Protocol channel, built to carry one final Earth transmission, carries forty-one voices instead. POV Oscar. Beat: climax; inheritance spent, not kept.

chapters.title: The Loop Ends
chapters.summary: The Protocol expires mid-broadcast — but the transmission is already propagating through every relay it ever touched, unrecallable, like the language itself. Hale orders a jam that arrives too late. POV Hale. Beat: catharsis; the machine outlives its masters.

chapters.title: Aftermath at Vespergate
chapters.summary: Freed dockworkers re-crew Vespergate as a memorial and listening post. Maren names the hall for her sister; Dree, released in the ensuing scandal, takes a cut of nothing and likes it. POV Maren. Beat: mourning turned to foundation.

chapters.title: Hale's Certification
chapters.summary: Hale, under inquiry, does the one honest act available: he certifies the massacre's record as genuine, using his master seal — the system's own instrument forced to tell the truth. His motives stay unreadable. POV Hale. Beat: ambiguous grace; power acknowledging its corruption.

chapters.title: The Underhill License
chapters.summary: Corvane collapses into inquiry; the family license is revoked. Oscar, professionally dead and personally free, signs over his remaining claim on the Vespergate case to Ilse — inheritance redirected. POV Oscar. Beat: resolution of the inheritance theme; the debt paid forward.

chapters.title: A Language With Speakers
chapters.summary: Months later, Ilse teaches High Meridian to the station's children while Oscar hauls cargo again, unlicensed, unbothered. A new signal arrives in the old tongue — and this time, people answer. POV Ilse. Beat: hopeful coda; justice as a living practice, not a verdict.
